key_insight: Long-range interactions let digital-analog quantum neural networks match short-range models on supervised tasks with fewer layers or shorter evolution times.
engineering_relevance: Combining single-qubit gates with long-range analog entanglement can reduce circuit resources and classical optimization overhead, potentially easing experimental implementation.
method: Interleave digital single-qubit operations with analog Ising evolution using power-law interactions.
Analyze how interaction range affects expressibility and trainability, alongside transverse field and evolution time.
Benchmark supervised image classification and many-body phase detection, plus unsupervised phase detection.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports supervised resource savings and complementary long- and short-range signatures that jointly reconstruct the complete phase diagram in unsupervised detection, but provides no numerical metrics.
watch_item: Long-range ansatzes do not outperform short-range counterparts in every unsupervised regime, so benefits remain task- and regime-dependent.
paper_title: Digital-Analog Quantum Neural Network with Long-Range Interactions
